title: Organizational Chart

illustrates.quote: For our purposes, an organizational chart is a diagram of the structure and/or personnel of an organization. The principal parts or functions are represented by blocks connected by lines to show hierarchical rank or interrelationships. Transcribe such material using a nested list format (1-5, 3-5; 1-7, 3-7, 5-7; etc.).

figure.description: Organizational chart of military ranks: a General at the top, two Colonels beneath, three Captains beneath them, two Sergeants and two Privates further down.

print.notes: The 'Sample 6-8: Organizational Chart' page heading (present in both runs' print.blocks) is not part of the excerpted braille (which starts directly at 'General') and is dropped, matching the across-the-section convention (see README). This sample has no transcriber's note and no figure caption/description beyond the chart itself. Every level is a single line (no runover anywhere), and no marriage/devised symbols or scripts are involved — unlike sample-6-5/6-6/6-7, this file is expected to be fully buildable.
print.printFeatures: A hierarchical organizational chart of boxes connected by lines.

braille.notes: 5-level nested list (1-3, 3-5, 5-7, 7-9, 9-11 margins per 6.9.1's nested-list convention), every item a single line. 'B' and 'C' each carry UEB's letter indicator (';') since a standalone lowercase 'b'/'c' would otherwise read as the whole-word contractions 'but'/'can'; 'A' needs none, since 'a' is not one of UEB's single-letter word signs — confirmed this is automatic in Emboss's own translator, not something print.blocks needs to encode.

resolution: B's braille.lines (margins stripped by 5 extra columns relative to A) match the raw source exactly (source-6.txt lines 5011-5020, decoded directly); A's margins are short by 2 cells at every level. The 'Sample 6-8: Organizational Chart' heading block both runs included is dropped (not part of the excerpted braille, matching the across-the-section convention); the empty figure `text`/`features` fields both runs left blank are removed as noise. print.blocks[1] built as a plain 5-level nested list directly from the chart's own hierarchy (General -> Colonel A/B -> Captain A/B/C -> Sergeant A/B -> Private A/B), reconstructed from the given indentation and figure.labels together, since neither run supplied the list structure itself (only the flat figure.labels array).
